title: feat(token-cost): attempt identity on TokenCostEvent for join accuracy
body:
# feat(token-cost): attempt identity on TokenCostEvent for join accuracy

## Background

Parent roadmap: #2296

Refs #2418, #2425 (non-blocking)

#2418 fixed `token-cost-harvest.mts`'s event-window join (used when a
Claude session log's `cwd` never varies, so cwd-based attribution is
structurally inert) to correlate a session's own record timestamps
against `token-cost-event.mjs`'s per-issue `enter`/`exit` windows
instead. That fix closed several concrete contamination bugs found
across its review rounds: reversed cleanup pairing, later-retry-stage
absorption, cross-file ambiguity, and — in its final round — a reversed
non-`cleanup` stage window (one attempt's `--enter` paired by
`readEventWindows`'s latest-wins semantics with an EARLIER, unrelated
attempt's stale `--exit`) is now detected and causes the whole issue to
be skipped for that harvest rather than emitting a silently-narrowed or
contaminated window.

That detection only catches the case where the stale pairing happens to
come out reversed (`startMs > endMs`). `TokenCostEvent` carries no
attempt/session identity at all in practice — every event is tagged only
by `(issueNumber, vendor, stageId, at, event)` — so a stale, EARLIER
attempt's enter/exit pair for some non-`cleanup` stage that happens to
still be internally VALID (non-reversed) is mechanically
indistinguishable from a genuine early start for the completed attempt.
This can happen when `token-cost-event.mjs`'s deliberately fail-open
posting (Refs `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` "Ignore any failure from this
command") drops BOTH of a later attempt's own enter/exit calls for one
stage, leaving the earlier attempt's own self-consistent pair as the
only value `readEventWindows` ever sees for that key. The resulting
`buildCompletedIssueWindows` union would silently widen `startMs` back
to the unrelated earlier attempt, absorbing usage from both attempts and
the intervening gap into one completed-loop sample under a stable
`#ew<issueNumber>` id, with no way to detect or correct it later.

Separately, `scanClaudeVendorSessions`'s cross-file event-window
fallback (also from #2418) currently resolves an issue number that
matches candidates from more than one log file by skipping the issue
entirely for that harvest (logging a warning) rather than picking a
side. #2419 empirically confirmed this is a real, dominant-not-rare
under-count on this workstation (10 of 12 completed issue-loop windows
blocked by it). #2425 investigated a disjoint-time-range merge for this
case and **rejected it before shipping**: a single sparse-record file
from an unrelated concurrent session can never register a wall-clock
"overlap" by definition, so a disjoint-only merge would absorb it just
as readily as a genuine continuation — the exact misattribution #2418's
own cross-file guard exists to prevent. #2425 shipped classification-only
diagnostics instead (still skips every cross-file match, but the stderr
warning now distinguishes "overlapping activity ranges" from "disjoint
activity ranges -- resolvable once events carry session identity,
#2424"), leaving this issue as the actual fix for the cross-file case,
not a residual-hardening follow-up to it.

`schemas/token-cost-event.schema.json` already declares an unused
`vendorSessionId` field on `TokenCostEvent` — no prior work ever stamps
it. `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` (a real environment variable, verified
present on this workstation) matches the current session's own
`~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<id>.jsonl` basename exactly — the
same value `extractSessionId()` (in `token-cost-adapter-claude.mts`)
already reads back out of a session log's own records. This closes the
loop deterministically for the Claude vendor with **no schema change**:
stamp `vendorSessionId` on every `token-cost-event.mjs` call from the
env var already available in-process, and match it against each
candidate file's own `extractSessionId()` result during cross-file
resolution.

## Proposed change

Populate the existing (currently unused) `vendorSessionId` field on
`TokenCostEvent` in `src/scripts/token-cost-event.mts`: derive it from
`$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` when present (Claude only for this issue --
Codex/Grok have no verified equivalent env var yet, matching #2418's
own single-vendor-at-a-time precedent) and stamp it on every
`enter`/`exit` call. No caller-facing change is needed: this is an
env-var auto-derive inside the helper itself, not a new CLI flag, so no
`CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`/`GEMINI.md`/`.github/copilot-instructions.md`
dogfood-invocation-example edit is required.

Update `readEventWindows` (`token-cost-harvest.mts`) so that, when a
stage's candidate enter/exit events carry a `vendorSessionId`, pairing
happens within that identity rather than via today's pure latest-wins
selection across the whole file. Update `buildCompletedIssueWindows` so
a non-`cleanup` stage window is only used to widen the completed
window's `startMs` when it is "id-compatible" with the winning
`cleanup` window -- and that compatibility check is deliberately
ASYMMETRIC, not "either side lacks an identity": a stage window is
compatible when its own `vendorSessionId` matches cleanup's, OR when
the STAGE window itself lacks an identity (predates this field, or a
vendor with no session-id source). An identified stage window is NEVER
compatible with an UNIDENTIFIED cleanup, even though the reverse
(identified cleanup, unidentified stage) is -- `vendorSessionId` is
derived once per process lifetime, so an identified stage and an
unidentified cleanup can never legitimately be the same attempt, while
an unidentified stage next to an identified cleanup is the ordinary
deploy-transition case. Where compatibility can't be determined either
way (both sides unidentified), the existing #2418 timestamp-only guards
keep applying exactly as today -- unchanged fallback, not a removed
check.
Update `scanClaudeVendorSessions`'s event-window candidate resolution
(both the multi-file case and the length-1 fast path) to require, when
the window carries a `vendorSessionId`, that the chosen candidate file's
own `extractSessionId()` equals it -- a SOLE candidate is not
automatically correct once identity can prove it wrong (e.g. this loop's
own session file got excluded upstream by the cwd-inferred-segment
guard, leaving only an unrelated concurrent session as the only
candidate). Continue to skip (with #2425's existing classification
message for the multi-file case, and a parallel one for the length-1
case) when no candidate matches, and continue to harvest a sole
candidate unconditionally when the window carries no identity
(unchanged from #2418/#2425).

Do not remove or weaken the #2418 guards (reversed-cleanup rejection,
half-open boundary matching, cross-file ambiguity skip) — this issue
adds a stronger signal on top of them for identified events, and they
remain the only signal for events that predate this field.

PR #2423 review also raised, and rejected, a related shape: a valid
(non-reversed) non-`cleanup` stage window whose `endMs` lands after
`cleanup.endMs` (e.g. a late-posted `--exit` catch-up call). That is
already excluded from widening `startMs` by the existing union check
and does not affect `buildCompletedIssueWindows`'s emitted bounds
today. With attempt identity available, this shape becomes cleanly
resolvable either way (same-attempt jitter when identities match, a
mismatched/excluded candidate otherwise) instead of the
timestamp-indistinguishable case it was under #2418 alone. Include a
regression test for this straddling shape (a stage window that starts
before and ends after the completed run's `cleanup.endMs`) alongside
the tests this issue already requires.

**Expected result after merge**: every historical event in
`events.jsonl` -- including this very issue's own claim/work-enter
events, posted from the pre-fix script -- has no `vendorSessionId`.
`docs/token-cost-snapshot.json`'s `sampleCount` is expected to stay at
`0` immediately after this PR merges; only IDD loops that *start* after
the merge produce identified events, so a real n>0 sample needs a
follow-up harvest after at least one full post-merge loop completes
(tracked separately, not a blocker for this issue's own tests/CI).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `token-cost-event.mts`/`.mjs` stamps the existing
      `vendorSessionId` field (no schema change) from
      `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` on every `enter`/`exit` call it emits,
      leaving the field absent when the env var is unset.
- [ ] `readEventWindows` pairs `enter`/`exit` within the same
      `vendorSessionId` when both events carry one, rather than
      latest-wins across the whole file; behavior for events lacking
      the field is unchanged from today.
- [ ] `buildCompletedIssueWindows` only widens `startMs` using a
      non-`cleanup` stage window that is id-compatible with the winning
      `cleanup` window -- compatible when the STAGE window's own
      `vendorSessionId` matches cleanup's, or when the stage window
      itself lacks an identity; an identified stage is NEVER compatible
      with an unidentified cleanup (asymmetric, not "either side lacks
      an identity"). Falls back to the existing #2418 timestamp-only
      guards when neither side carries an identity.
- [ ] `scanClaudeVendorSessions`'s event-window candidate resolution --
      both the multi-file case and the single-candidate fast path --
      requires the chosen file's own `extractSessionId()` to equal the
      window's `vendorSessionId` when the window has one, continuing to
      skip (per #2425's classification message, or a parallel one for
      the single-candidate case) when no candidate matches, and still
      harvesting a sole candidate unconditionally when the window has no
      identity.
- [ ] `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run build`, and `pnpm test` pass with
      new/updated unit tests covering: two attempts for the same issue
      with distinct identities (no cross-attempt contamination), an
      event with no identity field (historical-data fallback path), the
      straddling-window shape from PR #2423 review, a cross-file match
      resolved by identity, and a single-candidate match REJECTED
      because its `extractSessionId()` does not match the window's
      identity.
- [ ] `pnpm run lint` passes (includes `build:check` parity between
      `src/**/*.mts` and generated `scripts/`/`bin/*.mjs`).
- [ ] `docs/token-cost.md` documents the `vendorSessionId` field's
      purpose and the Claude-only-for-now scope.

below the configured floor is human-oriented._
